documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M (turned 23 last month) for physical.

Since last year: April crash as a passenger with R posterior hip dislocation, reduced in the ED, recovered fully per ortho, full duty since May. No hip symptoms.
ADHD: methylphenidate ER 36 qAM, works well. Sertraline 50 - mood mostly fine, a bit more stressed this summer with long hours. Headaches unchanged.
Habits: about a pack a day for 4+ years. Drinking 2-3 nights a week, 5-6 drinks. Says he wears his seatbelt now.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well, no distress. HEENT nl. Neck no LAD. Heart RRR no m/r/g. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abd benign. Hips: full painless ROM both sides. Skin clear. Neuro intact.
PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 4, AUDIT-C 8.

A/P:
- Flu and updated COVID vaccines today.
- CBC, CMP.
- Mood - mild stress, PHQ-9 still low; continue sertraline 50, he does not want a change.
- Tobacco - counseled, offered patch, declines.
- Alcohol - counseled, especially no drinking and driving and no riding with anyone who has been drinking. He says he gets it.
- ADHD - stable, continue.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Josue - labs from Tuesday look good. Blood count normal, kidney and liver tests normal, sugar normal. No changes needed. Hope the arm isn't sore from the shots.

events.reason: Head injury after motor vehicle collision

conditions.label: Diffuse traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness of unspecified duration, initial encounter
conditions.note: Diffuse axonal injury on CT, GCS 13 on arrival

reports.text:
Indication: high-speed MVC, loss of consciousness, GCS 13.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head with bone and soft tissue reconstructions.
Findings: multiple tiny punctate foci of hemorrhage scattered in the cerebral white matter, with blurring of the gray-white matter junction. No extra-axial collection. No large intraparenchymal hematoma. No midline shift. Ventricles and basal cisterns normal in size and configuration. No skull fracture. Paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear. Forehead soft tissue swelling.
reports.conclusion: Numerous punctate hemorrhages with blurred gray-white junction, consistent with diffuse axonal injury. No skull fracture or large intracranial hematoma.

reports.text:
Indication: follow-up of diffuse axonal injury.
Comparison: CT head 12/04/2025.
Findings: the small punctate hemorrhagic foci are unchanged in number and size. No new hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles stable. No skull fracture.
reports.conclusion: Stable appearance of punctate hemorrhages. No new intracranial hemorrhage.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Trauma Surgery. Admitted 12/04/2025, discharged 12/07/2025. Received 01/08/2026 after records request.

Admitting diagnosis: traumatic brain injury after MVC.
Discharge diagnosis: diffuse axonal injury.

History: 23 yo man brought in after a high-speed crash; unrestrained driver, lost consciousness at the scene per EMS. Background of ADHD and a mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome, and an ED visit in April 2025 for a right posterior hip dislocation.
Arrival: BP 130/85, HR 102, RR 18, T 37.1. GCS 13 - confused, agitated, not oriented. Abrasion across the forehead, no other external injury. Pupils equal, reactive. Moving all four limbs, no focal neurologic deficit.
CT head: multiple small punctate hemorrhages with loss of gray-white distinction, no fracture or large hematoma - diffuse axonal injury. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

Course: admitted to trauma ICU for hourly neuro checks. Repeat CT head next morning stable. Neurosurgery reviewed images, no operative need. Mental status cleared, GCS 15 by afternoon of 12/05. Transferred to floor 12/06. Ambulating independently, tolerating diet. Home methylphenidate held while inpatient, resumed at discharge.

Discharge meds: methylphenidate ER 36 mg qAM, sertraline 50 mg daily, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn headache.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no driving and no return to work until cleared at follow-up. Rest, limited screens first days, gradual return to activity. Avoid alcohol. Return for worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, weakness or seizure. Follow up with PCP within 1 week; outpatient neurology/brain injury clinic referral recommended.
Discharged home with family.

documents.title: Call from mother - hospital discharge
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Patient's mother called (pt with her, gave verbal ok to speak with her). He was in another car accident Thursday night, he was driving. Hit his head, kept in the ICU then the floor, discharged yesterday. They said there was bleeding "in small spots" in the brain. No surgery. At home he has a headache and is sleeping a lot but is making sense, eating, walking fine. No vomiting. Discharge papers say see PCP in a week.
Reviewed red flags: worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness, seizure -> 911/ED. Booked with PCP Thu 12/11. Asked them to bring discharge paperwork.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M, here with his mother, 4 days after discharge from a 12/4-12/7 admission after a second high-speed crash (this time he was the driver, not belted). Only the patient instructions sheet came with him; no discharge summary yet.
Per the sheet and family: lost consciousness at the scene, CT showed diffuse axonal injury (small bleeds), ICU overnight, repeat CT stable, no surgery, back to normal thinking the next day.

Now: headaches most days since discharge, ibuprofen takes the edge off. Tired, napping. Can follow a TV show but focus fades by late afternoon. No vomiting, no vision change, no weakness, no seizure. Methylphenidate restarted at discharge. Sertraline continued. Not driving. Not drinking since.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Alert, oriented x3, answers appropriately, a bit slow. Healing abrasion forehead, no swelling. Pupils equal, reactive. EOMI, no nystagmus. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 all limbs, reflexes symmetric, finger-nose normal, gait steady, Romberg negative. GCS 15.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury after MVC 12/4 - recovering, nonfocal exam. Added to problem list. Relative rest with gradual return to activity; ibuprofen prn, limit to a few days a week to avoid rebound. No driving until neurology clears him. Off work until early January - note given. Neurology referral placed. Requesting the hospital records.
2. Post-concussive syndrome (from age 19) - expect headaches to be worse for a while.
3. ADHD - continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg.
4. Alcohol - strongly advised to stay off alcohol while the brain heals; he says he will.
5. Seatbelt.
RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Josue Hernandez is under my care following a hospitalization. He is unable to work through 01/04/2026. I expect he can return to light duty on 01/05/2026, with no work at heights or with live circuits until further notice. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: Headaches question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: headaches are getting better, maybe every other day now and not as bad. still get tired in the afternoon. is it still ok to go back the 5th? my foreman said they can keep me on the ground doing material and prep.

documents.title: RE: Headaches question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's the direction we want. Yes, light duty on the ground from 1/5 is fine - no ladders, lifts or live work yet, and take breaks when the fatigue hits. No driving until neurology sees you. The neurology office should call you to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard by the first week of January.

documents.title: Back at work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: first day back went ok. tired but fine. neuro appt is Feb 4. thanks

documents.title: RE: Back at work
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks for the update, Josue - noted for the doctor. Keep that Feb 4 appointment.

documents.title: Hospital records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Discharge summary and both CT head reports from the December admission received today (requested 12/11). Diffuse axonal injury, GCS 13 on arrival, stable repeat CT, GCS 15 next day, no surgery. Matches what the family described. No other injuries listed. Nothing new to act on.

documents.title: Methylphenidate refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: need my adhd med refill please, due thursday

documents.title: RE: Methylphenidate refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent, PMP checked. How did the neurology visit go? I haven't received their note yet - please ask them to send it, or tell me at your March visit.

documents.title: Office Visit - TBI follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up 3 months after the December diffuse axonal injury.
Neurology: seen once, early February. No note has come to us despite the request. Per patient, they told him he was recovering well, could go back to full duty and could drive again. Full duty since late February.
Headaches back to his old pattern, a couple a month, ibuprofen prn. Energy normal. Focus back to where it was on methylphenidate. Mood ok. Back to drinking on weekends, 5-6 when he goes out. Smoking a pack daily.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, oriented, conversational, quick. Forehead healed. CN II-XII intact, strength and coordination normal, gait and tandem normal.
PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 8.

A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury 12/2025 - back to baseline, marking resolved. Neurology referral closed on his report.
2. Post-concussive syndrome - unchanged, continue sertraline 50 and ibuprofen prn.
3. ADHD - continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg.
4. Alcohol and tobacco - two serious crashes in a year. Long talk about drinking, driving, seatbelts. Offered referral again; he will think about it.
RTC 3 mo (video ok).

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - medication check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, ID confirmed.
No new issues. Methylphenidate ER 36 working, no side effects. Mood fine. Headaches infrequent. Working full time.
Still smoking, still drinking on weekends - declines help today.
Plan: continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg and sertraline 50 mg. PMP checked. Physical in the fall.

reports.text:
Indication: MVC, unresponsive, GCS 6.
Comparison: CT head 12/05/2025.
Findings: no acute intracranial hemorrhage. No extra-axial collection. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No sulcal effacement, no cerebral edema. Ventricles and cisterns normal. No midline shift. No skull fracture.
reports.conclusion: No skull fracture, intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral edema.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. DOS 08/02/2026. Received 08/20/2026 in response to records request. Inpatient records not included.

CC: MVC, unresponsive.
HPI: 23 yo M, unrestrained driver in a high-speed collision with extensive driver-side damage per EMS. Unresponsive on EMS arrival and on ours. Hx per chart: ADHD; diffuse axonal injury 12/2025; mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome; R posterior hip dislocation 4/2025. Meds methylphenidate ER, sertraline, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

Primary survey: airway not protected, GCS 6. Intubated on arrival for airway protection, rapid sequence, first pass, tube position confirmed.
Secondary: pupils equal and reactive. No palpable skull fracture or scalp step-off. No lateralizing findings. Chest, abdomen and pelvis without external trauma.
CT head: no fracture, no hemorrhage, no edema. CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Course: despite the negative CT he remains comatose off sedation pauses, with intermittent decerebrate posturing. Neurosurgery and trauma consulted.
Impression: severe traumatic brain injury, clinical picture of diffuse axonal injury with normal CT.
Disposition: admitted to trauma ICU 04:35, intubated.
